title: Harmonic-extension Schur capacity decomposition of phase-conditioned graph gaps
question: Can the phase-conditioned intrinsic graph be decomposed by an exact harmonic extension and Schur complement, so that within-block coercivity and the coarse inter-block capacity give a valid lower bound without the false naive block-gap shortcut?

new_perspective.principle: Use the Dirichlet principle rather than the Ritz restriction: fix the conditional block means, minimize the graph energy by harmonic extension, and retain the orthogonal residual as a separate coercive sector.
route: Normalize each conditional law pi and form A=diag(pi)^(-1/2)Ldiag(pi)^(-1/2) from the intrinsic momentum conductance.
Let U be the weighted block-constant subspace for lower, neutral and upper q sectors and V its Euclidean orthogonal complement.
Eliminate V by the Schur complement S=A_UU-A_UV A_VV^(-1) A_VU; the positive spectrum of S on the global-mean-zero coarse space is the harmonic coarse capacity gap.
The residual gap is the least eigenvalue of A_VV. Orthogonality of the harmonic correction gives an exact energy and variance split, hence a finite lower bound min(coarse gap,residual gap).
Compute the uncorrected block-constant Ritz gap as a hostile comparison: it is an upper restriction value and can exceed the full gap, so it cannot be used as a lower bound.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: An analytic version would supply a phase-conditioned common-core estimate by proving uniform lower bounds for the Schur coarse operator and the zero-block-mean residual form. The Schur capacity is the precise finite interface to the inter-phase selection/tunnelling debt; it is not itself a phase-selection or GNS theorem.

finite_theorem.weighted_operator: A=diag(pi)^(-1/2)Ldiag(pi)^(-1/2), with L the symmetric intrinsic momentum graph Laplacian.
finite_theorem.harmonic_extension: For coarse coordinate z in the weighted block-constant subspace, w_h=-A_VV^(-1)A_VU z minimizes y^T A y over U^T y=z.
finite_theorem.schur_operator: S=A_UU-A_UV A_VV^(-1)A_VU; its first positive eigenvalue on the global-mean-zero coarse space is kappa_coarse.
finite_theorem.residual_operator: The first eigenvalue of A_VV is kappa_residual for block-mean-zero fluctuations.
finite_theorem.finite_bound: E(f) >= min(kappa_coarse,kappa_residual) Var_pi(f) on the centered finite graph, after the harmonic/residual orthogonal split.
finite_theorem.shortcut_warning: The block-constant restriction gap is a Ritz upper value for the full gap, not a lower bound; the Schur correction is required.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks scalar square/variance bookkeeping only; Schur spectra, Gibbs rows, graph limits, common domains and QFT reconstruction remain executable/open analysis.

promotion_criteria: Prove source-, cutoff-, volume- and exhaustion-uniform lower bounds for the Schur coarse operator and residual form on one Hamiltonian common core.
Identify the Schur coarse variables with a justified phase boundary condition and control neutral mass and cross-sector capacity under the limit.
Transfer the centered harmonic/residual split to the R-399 shell and then discharge the common-alpha and broken-sector GNS gates.
stop_conditions: If the Schur coarse or residual gap collapses under a validated cutoff/volume stress, retain the decomposition only as a diagnostic and do not claim phasewise coercivity.
If the block-constant shortcut exceeds the full gap, keep the Schur correction mandatory; never use a Ritz restriction as a lower bound.
Finite Schur positivity is not a common-core, phase-selection, GNS, QFT or mass-gap theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite harmonic-extension/Schur-complement checkpoint only. It proves no uniform sector gap, phase selection, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The Schur decomposition is an exact finite variational interface and a correction to a false shortcut. Its constants are not promoted to regulator or thermodynamic bounds.
